subject: Signature ops: migration impact & cost-risk note
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@ironclad.com>, David Li <d.li@docusign.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Signature ops: migration impact & cost-risk note

Hi Emily, David —

We’re running a short procurement sprint to decide whether to consolidate e-signing and contract signature workflows under one vendor (DocuSign) or move signature-only to Ironclad’s signing module as part of a larger CLM transition. Attached is the RFP summary and scope (redwood-rfp-esign.pdf).

Key asks:
- High-level migration timeline (weeks) and required Redwood internal effort for a signature-only migration vs full CLM migration.
- One-time migration costs and annual run-rate for both approaches.
- Known feature gaps (for example, in-person signing, embedded signing, Zapier/webhook parity, and API rate limits).
- Data residency / audit log differences and contract data export formats.

We need initial numbers by EOD tomorrow so Legal + Finance can model budget impact for Q4.

Thanks — appreciate concise bullet answers.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-rfp-esign.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@ironclad.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Signature ops: migration impact & cost-risk note

On 2027-07-11 09:02, Avery Johnson wrote:
> We’re running a short procurement sprint…

Hi Avery / team —

Thanks for the RFP. I attached a short proposal and a one-page migration plan (ironclad-proposal-Q3.pdf). High-level answers below:

- Migration timeline: signature-only via Ironclad Authenticated Signing can be completed in ~6 weeks (3 weeks integration + 3 weeks QA/consumer testing) assuming access to a staging tenant and 2 FTEs from Redwood for mapping existing templates and webhooks.
- One-time costs: onboarding + migration estimate = $75k (includes template mapping, webhook migration, custom connector work).
- Annual run-rate: $0.18 per signature event at our listed volume band; for 1M signatures/year we’d price at $180k/yr (discounts available with 12mo commit).
- Feature gaps: Ironclad supports embedded signing + audit logs; current limitations are fewer native marketplace integrations compared to DocuSign (we provide webhook-first integrations). In-person signing (kiosk mode) is available via partner connector (additional $10k).
- Data residency & export: exports are JSON/CSV via API and we provide a monthly audit export for compliance. SOC2 docs and a summary of retention controls are attached.

If you want, we can run a short demo and a migration pilot (10 templates) next week.

Regards,
Emily Park
Strategic Accounts — Ironclad
Attachments: ironclad-proposal-Q3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); ironclad-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 140KB)

From: David Li <d.li@docusign.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Signature ops: migration impact & cost-risk note

Avery —

Appreciate the heads up. Short reply with counterpoints from our side:

- Migration timeline (keeping DocuSign): zero migration effort for e-sign, we can export usage metrics + offer a template rationalization sprint (2 weeks) to reduce cost.
- One-time costs: if you stay on DocuSign we can provide a discounted package for consolidated templates and add a free migration toolkit for the next 90 days.
- Annual run-rate: we can offer $0.14 per signature at the 1M band (subject to commitment); we’ll provide a formal quote and an updated SOW.
- Feature parity: DocuSign has broader marketplace integrations, native in-person signing, and a well-established audit trail format.
- Compliance: SOC2 + enterprise audit logs available; will share current SOC2 cert and encryption details on request.

I attached a redlined SOW from our commercial team for the consolidation approach (docusign-sow-redline.docx). Happy to jump on a call to walk through tradeoffs — we think consolidation reduces overall program risk.

Thanks,
David Li
Enterprise Sales
DocuSign
Attachments: docusign-sow-redline.docx (Word, 320KB)

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Signature ops: migration impact & cost-risk note

Team — quick internal summary following vendor replies above and attachments:

- Ironclad: cleaner path if we intend to migrate full CLM in 12–18 months (single vendor for contract lifecycle + signing). Estimated 6-week signature pilot, $75k one-time, $180k/yr at scale. Minor integration work and partner connector needed for in-person signing.
- DocuSign: lowest disruption path; can keep all signing in-place, offer a lower per-signature rate ($0.14 with commit) and a template rationalization program; minimal internal effort.

Principal decision levers: near-term operational disruption (low for DocuSign), medium-term strategic alignment with CLM roadmap (Ironclad), and TCO over 3 years (we need numbers from Finance modeled into the attached spreadsheet).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Finance to run 3-year TCO using the attached cost-comparison-spreadsheet.xlsx (Neha, can you own?)
2) Legal to validate exports/audit trails and confirm retention policy compatibility with Redwood compliance (Marissa, can you own vendor SOC2 intake?)
3) Procurement to run a 2-week pilot with chosen vendor for 10 high-volume templates (I’ll schedule after we get TCO numbers).

Please reply with confirmations on owners and any blockers by EOD Friday.

Avery
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cost-comparison-spreadsheet.xlsx (Excel, 95KB)
